title: refactor(rest): move registerSecurityExplainEndpoints and registerSecurityEndpoints into security-routes.ts (#23050 slice 6)
body:
Part of #23050
Clause-②: no

Slice 6 of the `rest-server.ts` split, by slice 1's pattern (landed note `6136102437`, steps 1–6), slice 2's getter refinement (`6189011700`) and slices 3–5's shape (PR #23670, PR #23705's two registrars in one module, PR #23719): the bodies of `RestServer#registerSecurityExplainEndpoints` (`GET` / `POST {basePath}/security/explain`, `GET {basePath}/security/my-delegable-scope`) and `RestServer#registerSecurityEndpoints` (`GET {basePath}/security/suggested-bindings` and its `/:id/confirm` and `/:id/dismiss`) move, unedited, to ONE new module, `packages/rest/src/security-routes.ts`. It is move-only: routes, the ordered registrations, every handler, the published `dist/*.d.ts` and both bundles' export lists are byte-identical, and every reader whose reading included a moved line now reads it where it is, with its sum unchanged.

`rest-server.ts` goes from 11,042 to 10,636 lines (base `a515abdd8c`). The card stays open for the later slices.

## The pattern, applied

**Members the moved bodies read**, from an AST walk of each method (TypeScript compiler API, base `a515abdd8c`): `registerSecurityExplainEndpoints` (JSDoc `:10282`, method `:10308`-`:10601`, body `:10309`-`:10600`) and `registerSecurityEndpoints` (JSDoc `:10662`, method `:10694`-`:10838`, body `:10695`-`:10837`).

| kind | member | reads (explain / suggested-binding) | class declaration |
|---|---|---|---|
| field | `routeManager` | 3 / 3, the `register` calls | `:2010`, private |
| field | `kernelManager` | 2 / 0, inside the explain family's `resolveService` | `:2019`, private, not `readonly` |
| field | `securityServiceProvider` | 2 / 2, inside each family's `resolveService` | `:2089`, private, not `readonly` |
| method | `resolveRequestEnvironmentId` | 1 / 0 | `:2306`, private |
| method | `resolveExecCtx` | 2 / 3 | `:2856`, private |
| method | `enforceAuth` | 2 / 3 | `:2456`, private |

Neither body has a bare `this`, an element access on `this`, or a `this`-rebinding `function`. Their module-level reads:

- **Imports still used elsewhere in `rest-server.ts`** (AST count outside both methods): `logError` (12), `sendError as sendEnvelopeError` (4) and `refuseRepeatedQueryParams` (15). They stay there; the module imports the same names from the same modules. Its `sendError` import carries a comment pointing at the dialect note on `rest-server.ts`'s import, which the explain family's emitter docblock names.
- **Imports ONLY these bodies read** (zero uses outside the two methods): `ErrorCode` (type, `@objectstack/spec/api`, with its `[#8073]` comment), `standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus` (`@objectstack/spec/api`, `[#11683]`), `classifiedRefusalAnswer`, `nestedRefusalEnvelope`, `sandboxFaultAnswer` (`./error-response.js`), and `isAudienceBindingSuggestionStatus` with `unknownAudienceBindingSuggestionStatusMessage` (`@objectstack/core`, `[#7678]`). They moved with the bodies, as slices 3 and 5 moved theirs, and each left a pointer comment. Leaving them would fail `noUnusedLocals`. The `[#8073]` and `[#7678]` comments moved verbatim. The `[#11683]` comment pointed at `registerSharingEndpoints` as its use, so in the module it names the explain family's classified-refusal arm, the use it has there.
- **Nothing declared in `rest-server.ts` is read**, so no `export` was added anywhere. The explain body's dynamic `import('@objectstack/spec/security')` moved inside it.

**Host shape (slice 1's shape B, twice, as slice 4):** one host interface per registrar, `SecurityExplainRouteHost` and `SecurityRouteHost`. Each lists exactly the members its body reads, typed `RestServer['m']`. The class keeps both private methods with their names, docblocks and positions. Each body is now a host literal plus `.call(host, basePath)`. Methods go as late-bound closures, `(...a) => this.m(...a)`. The call sites in `registerRoutes` (`:4812`-`:4813` at base) are unchanged.

**Fields, checked one by one:**

| field | read when | reassigned after registration? | handed over as |
|---|---|---|---|
| `routeManager` | registration only (six `register` calls, top-level statements of the two bodies) | its one swap (`:5719` / `:5723`) wraps `registerMetadataEndpointsInner`, not these registrars | value |
| `kernelManager` | **request time** (the explain family's `resolveService`) | not by the class (constructor only), but not `readonly` | **getter** |
| `securityServiceProvider` | **request time** (each family's `resolveService`) | not by the class (constructor only), but not `readonly` | **getter**, in both host literals |

The getters are measured, not argued. A one-off vitest file (copied in, run, deleted) boots a source `RestServer`, drives the door, assigns the field on the instance AFTER `registerRoutes()`, and drives it again:

- this head (`96504dab66`): `securityServiceProvider` on the explain family (`GET /api/v1/security/my-delegable-scope`) reads `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, then `200 {"businessUnits":["bu_1"],"positions":[]}`. On the suggested-binding family (`GET /api/v1/security/suggested-bindings`) it reads `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, then `200 {"data":[{"id":"sug_1"}]}`. `kernelManager` on the scoped explain door (`environmentId: env_1`) reads `501`, then `200 {"env":"env_1"}`. `Tests 3 passed (3)`.
- by-value ablations through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each getter in turn replaced by `X: this.X,` with a two-line anchor that names its host literal. Each landed: anchor 1 → 0, replacement 0 → 1, blob `4867a14302` → `5c7ebad6df` / `48f2660f00` / `f3c9b53365`. In each run the ablated door reads `501` then `501` (frozen at registration) while the other two still read `200` (`Tests 1 failed | 2 passed (3)`, each run). Restored by the tool and a trap: blob `4867a14302` equals `HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty, the one-off file deleted. The path is source (relative import), so no `dist` leg applies.

**Mechanism hypotheses from the dispatch, measured:**

- (a) **Confirmed.** The explain family resolves the security service at request time through its `resolveService`. That reads TWO fields: the environment kernel's `security` service via `kernelManager` first, then `securityServiceProvider` as the fallback. Naming a principal other than the caller is the service's question (`explainAccessForCaller`); the door hands it the parsed request and the caller's context and reads no further provider field. Both fields go as getters. The suggested-binding family reads `securityServiceProvider` only, also a getter, measured separately.
- (b) **Confirmed.** `registerSecurityEndpoints` builds its paths from `const dataPath = basePath;`, so the suggested-binding doors answer at `{basePath}/security/suggested-bindings`, not under `/data` (slice 4's share family appended `crud.dataPrefix`; this one does not). Every path expression moved unedited, and the route dumps below are identical.
- (c) **Confirmed.** The bodies, and the `[#7678]` import comment that moved with them, carry 10 `ADR-NNNN Dk` citations: ADR-0090 D5 ×2, D6 ×2 and D12 ×2, ADR-0105 D8 ×2, and ADR-0112 D5 ×2. They left the anchored `rest-server.ts`, so `check-adr-anchors` read 1761 decision-letter citations at base and 1751 at the move-only commit `d6fc91a97d`, **green both times**. That is the silent narrowing the card forbids. A new anchor (below) restores 1761 at head.

## The registrar list

`packages/rest/src/rest-server-registrar-files.ts` gains `security-routes.ts` with a `[#23050 slice 6]` comment (length 6 → 7). Every reader that pins its length re-reads its number, and every sum is unchanged:

| reader | sum over the list | change |

| `rest-server-query-number-census.test.ts` | 9 = 8 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 | length 6 → 7 |
| `rest-server-canonical-query-ast.test.ts` | 4 = 1 + 3 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 `query:` slots | floor `security-routes.ts: 0`, length 6 → 7 |
| `meta-draft-read-door-census.test.ts` | 8 = 6 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 2 + 0 | the two bodies read no draft; length 6 → 7 |
| `rest-server-docblock-position.test.ts` | floors 4 + 3 + 3 + 8 + 3 + 8 = 29 | floor `security-routes.ts: 8`: header, two host interfaces, two functions, and the three blocks that moved with the bodies (the explain family's `respondError` and `delegableHandler` blocks, the suggested-binding family's `respondError` block). `rest-server.ts` 167 → 164 blocks, floor 100; length 6 → 7 |
| `execctx-consumer-census.test.ts` | 62 sites = 27 + 9 + 5 + 7 + 8 + 1 + 5 | mentions 101 → 109 (the seam twice: two forwarders ×2, two interface members ×2); forwarders 8 = (7 − 1) + `EXTRA_MOVED_REGISTRARS` 2, the map gaining `security-routes.ts: 1` beside `sharing-routes.ts: 1`, as slice 4 counted two registrars in one module |
| `ui-view-route-identity.measurement.test.ts` / `ui-view-route-tenancy.measurement.test.ts` | `this.enforceAuth(` 55, `this.resolveExecCtx(` 70 over the list (53 / 68 before, +1 each per new forwarder); ownership guard 1 | length 6 → 7 |
| dogfood `authz-conformance.test.ts` (realtime tripwires) | 0 hits over the seven files | length 6 → 7 |
| dogfood `authz-probe-blind-spot.census.ts`, `rest-server.ts` row | 70 / 19 / 51 unchanged; `this.routeManager.register(` 63 = 27 + 9 + 5 + 7 + 8 + 1 + 6; `private register*Endpoints(` 16 | new control `security-routes.ts: this.routeManager.register(` 6; `registrar list length` 7; `enforceAuth` 84 → 92 re-anchored (five call sites moved and are counted in both readings; the eight new occurrences are the seam twice; no call site added); `populationRule` names the new module |

Each number above was also counted statically on the tree (`grep -oF` per file).

## Proof of move-only

- **`.d.ts`:** `packages/rest/dist/index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts` built at base `a515abdd8c` (this worktree, before any edit), at `96504dab66` and at the merge head `a12cdcf4e4` are byte-identical: sha256 `7489de84bc6feccb7cb1f28bcbe4a97775324959c61c9bfc35e8a8c45a6f3bc9` for all six files, `cmp` silent. The head bundles carry a head-only marker (`readSecurityServiceProvider`, 4 hits in each of `index.js` and `index.cjs`), so the declaration was rebuilt from the moved source, not replayed. `SecurityExplainRouteHost`, `SecurityRouteHost` and `security-routes` appear 0 times in the `.d.ts`; `src/index.ts` is untouched.
- **Export lists:** the base and head ESM and CJS bundles each load with 39 exports and one sorted export-name list (sha256 `b3246be6a171…` on all four), and none of the two functions or two host types is among them.
- **Routes:** a source `RestServer` on a recording mock server, with a protocol that answers every member, dumped under four configs at base and at head: `getRoutes()` (functions as arity), the ordered server registration calls, and a whitespace-free sha256 of every handler's source. **12 dumps of 12 are byte-identical**, at `96504dab66` and again at the merge head. default: routes `6931d1a5d182…`, calls `ccb3bd12f10b…`, handlers `6d4926ef1465…` (75 routes, 6 security); scoped-optional: `275c72f46c30…` / `339e8c3abc05…` / `92790e91927d…` (150, 12); scoped-required: `a2aa8183e213…` / `734f33133150…` / `f6e3fd853aea…` (75, 6); every-provider-set equals default. A second base run was identical to the first.
- **The handler digest can fail:** a positive control changed one character of one moved handler (`Delegable scope error:` → `!`, through `ablation-replace.mjs`; anchor 1 → 0, blob `01fe3b195d` → `0c2c62e946`). Routes and calls were unchanged, and the handler list differed in exactly `GET /api/v1/security/my-delegable-scope` (and its scoped twin). Restored, blob `01fe3b195d` equals `HEAD`.
- **Moved bodies:** base `rest-server.ts` lines 10309-10600 and 10695-10837, one 4-space indent removed, against `security-routes.ts` lines 110-401 and 411-553: `diff` exits 0 both times (292 + 143 lines). No moved line has an odd number of backticks, so no template literal spans the cut and re-indenting changes no runtime string.
- **Moved-line accounting:** `git diff --color-moved=plain --color-moved-ws=allow-indentation-change` base → move commit over the two files: 442 deleted and 470 added lines detected as moved. `rest-server.ts` is +43 / −449: the two stub bodies (host literal plus `.call`), the slice-6 import and its comment, and four import-pointer comments.

## Readers re-pointed (sums unchanged, no gate loosened)

- `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` (a gate's target paths, `domain:spec`): `security-routes.ts` is discovered by the `*-routes.ts` convention and declared `dialectOnly` with ratchet #9559, as the five earlier modules are, at its measured `stringError 0`, `siblingCode 0`. Every arm of both families emits the nested `{ error: { code, message } }` through its family's one emitter (the emitters #7981 and #8073 introduced). So `rest-server.ts` stays at `stringError 17`, `siblingCode 17`, and the sums 17 + 13 + 8 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 39 and 17 + 15 + 8 + 9 + 4 + 1 + 0 = 54 are unchanged. Output differs from base only in the new row (16 → 17 modules, 7 → 8 ratcheted). `--self-test` green.
- `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__rest__src__security-routes.ts.json` (**new**, ADR-0090 + ADR-0105 + ADR-0112): `check-adr-anchors` decision-letter citations on the anchored surface 1761 (base) → 1751 (move) → 1761 (head); anchored files 67 → 68. Every listed id appears in the module, and every cited letter is a decision of its record (the gate's own check, green). The invariant writes "its D6", never "ADR-0090 D6", so it adds no citation of its own (measured with the gate's regex: 0).
- The nine registrar-list readers above.
- `error-response.ts`, the `nestedRefusalEnvelope` docblock (rest lane, not in the published `.d.ts`): it named `rest-server.ts` as the home of three families, the suggested-binding one among them. Since slices 3, 4 and this one moved all three, the sentence now names each family's current home.

**Red before the re-points**, each measured with the move in place (`d6fc91a97d`): the six `local` list readers read `Test Files 6 failed (6)`, `Tests 7 failed | 103 passed (110)` (five length pins, plus the docblock pin's length pin and its new module with no floor). `rest-server-canonical-query-ast.test.ts` (`repo`) read `Tests 2 failed | 53 passed | 7 skipped (62)`. The dogfood pair read `Tests 2 failed | 106 passed (108)` (list length; the census row's `registrar list length` control). `tsc --noEmit` was clean, but `check:test-typecheck` found 2 type errors, the two typed floor tables without the new module. `check:route-envelope` read `security-routes.ts NOT DECLARED` (MODULES and EXPRESS_RESPONSE_MODULES). `check-adr-anchors` was green at 1751.

## Acceptance notes

- `rest-server.ts`'s `resolveSecurityService` docblock (about `:9506`) says it "Mirrors the resolver in registerSecurityExplainEndpoints". That docblock ships in the published `.d.ts`, so editing it would break the byte-identity this slice must keep. It is not edited, and the name still resolves to the function of that name in `security-routes.ts`, which holds the resolver.
- Other-lane prose that names `rest-server.ts` for the suggested-binding route, read by nothing: `packages/core/src/security/audience-binding-suggestion-status.ts` (about `:10`, and about `:18`, which says `rest-server.ts` imports the vocabulary; the importer is now `security-routes.ts`) and `packages/runtime/src/domains/security.ts` (about `:144`). Not edited (承接者:无).
- `docs/adr/0112-…`'s Consumers line names `rest-server.ts` for `@objectstack/rest` as a whole, not as these doors' home. It is a governed surface and is not edited.
- `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`'s count-history comments for `rest-server.ts` (the #7981 and #8073 entries) say the two registrars sat in that file when those counts moved. They are dated history, unchanged.
- `docs/adr/0076-…` (status line and D11) and `docs/adr/0111-…` (Consumers line) are still carried to the maintainer by the seat; this slice adds nothing to them.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run --project repo --maxWorkers=2`: Test Files 5 passed (5), Tests 234 passed / 7 skipped (241), at both heads.

Its one warning is `File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied` for the JSON, which `eslint .` never reads. All 15 changed files are in the result set at 0 / 0. The published `.d.ts` is byte-identical, so no consumer outside `packages/rest` can lint differently. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
